newsitem.title: USA: South Carolina committee okays tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: South Carolina committee okays tax cuts.

text.p: The South Carolina General Assembly's joint budget committee has approved major tax cuts for senior citizens and car owners.

One proposal approved Thursday would phase out income taxes over two years for residents age 65 and over. The tax would be eliminated this year for seniors earning less than $11,500 and would be eliminated entirely in 1998.
The cut is expected to cost the state $65 million over two years.
The committee also approved a proposal to phase out the state's property tax on motor vehicles by 2005.

The car tax is levied by cities, counties and school districts and will bring in about $408 million next year. Still pending is an agreement on when that cut would begin and how to compensate local governments.
Negotiators on the joint budget committee are working toward agreement on a $4.6 budget that would go to both chambers for an up-or-down vote before legislatures adjourn on June 5.
